newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai PM rules out resignation - spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Thai PM rules out resignation - spokesman.

text.p: Thailand's prime minister has ruled out speculation that he will either resign or dissolve parliament before the opposition grills him during a mid-week no-confidence debate, his spokesman said on Monday.
Premier Banharn Silpa-archa also rejected demands from critics that he step down in favour of a more acceptable politician, spokesman Somsak Prisana-anantakul added.
But he said that Banharn could bring in some of the other opposition parties into his six-party coalition to strengthen his administration and numbers in parliament.
Banharn faces a no-confidence motion that accuses him, among other things, of incompetence and economic mismanagement. The debate in parliament is due to begin on Wednesday and last a couple of days.
He has vowed to defend himself against the accusations.
"You can rule out the resignation or dissolving of the house. The Prime Minister said this morning that his government is not yet cornered," Somsak told reporters.
"He has many ways out from the current situation, and these include bringing (opposition) Chart Pattana and Seritham into the coalition," Somsak said after a meeting with Banharn.
The major opposition Chart Pattana Party has 54 seats and the Seritham 11 seats in the 391-seat parliament.
Although Banharn's 14-month-old goverment controls 209 seats in parliament, there have been demands by some coalition politicians for him to resign or lose their support.

The premier's coalition has been riddled with economic and political problems since he took power in July last year. The coalition has been wracked by internal rifts and attacked vehemently by a hostile local press.
On the economic front, the Thai stock index has dropped to near-three-year lows on poor economic indicators and rumours about the health of some finance and securities firms.

Thailand's once-high-flying and robust economy is slowing sharply, with many analysts expecting the growth of gross domestic product to fall below 7.0 percent this year from earlier higher projections and the 8.6 percent posted in 1995.
Growth in exports has slowed sharply to 3.8 percent in the first seven months of this year compared with 26.2 percent growth in the same year-ago period.

Former prime minister Chatichai Choonhavan, who now heads the Chart Pattana Party, had urged Banharn to resign last week. He also suggested that a new coalition be formed to lead the nation, without the dissolution of parliament.

Defense Minister General Chavalit Yongchaiyudh has hinted that his New Aspiration Party, the second largest in the coalition government with 57 seats, will support Banharn through the debate but could leave the coalition after that.
Both Chatichai and Chavalit have their eyes on the premiership and are leading contenders should Banhrn leave the post, political analysts said.
